title: Embed incident-derived safety belts and verifiable acceptance tests into runtime PRD
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: After the Sept 14 multi-region burst incident (SUR-2025-09-14) the postmortem defined five engineering mitigations and three operational changes. This ticket translates those postmortem actions into concrete PRD requirements, acceptance tests, and rollout gates so product, SRE, and engineering can ship changes with measurable safety guarantees. Deliverables: updated PRD text, a matrix of acceptance tests mapped to postmortem items, operator runbook hooks, and release gating criteria tied to telemetry thresholds.
background: During SUR-2025-09-14, a sudden burst of short-lived traffic sequences caused kernel saturation on a subset of serving nodes which cascaded into higher latencies and partial fallbacks. The postmortem recommended: deterministic fallback contracts, canary rollback criteria, synthetic tests for tail-latency, explicit operator remediation steps, and automated verification of fallback efficacy.
scope: This PRD update will: (1) codify the safety belts (fallback contracts, canary gates, rollback triggers), (2) define acceptance tests and synthetic scenarios, (3) specify telemetry/alerts and required dashboards, (4) list release gating criteria and manual checklists for operators, (5) provide a verification plan for Dedicated and Hosted variants.
out_of_scope: Changes to the low-level kernel implementation, new kernel patches, or on-prem packaging for Private customers. Those are tracked separately with ENG-owned tickets. Also, UI changes to Console are out of scope for this ticket (except links to new dashboards).
requirements: PRD must include a failover contract: for any latency spike >99th percentile delta of 150ms sustained for 5m, traffic must route to fallback model variant within 30s or trigger controlled rate-limit for affected tenants.
Define canary criteria: new kernel/serving changes require a canary serving at 1% traffic for 2hr with synthetic tail-latency < baseline + 50ms and no increase in error rate >0.05%.
Acceptance tests: three synthetic scenarios (surge short bursts, sustained moderate load, multi-tenant benign spike) with deterministic verification steps and automated pass/fail reporting.
Operator runbook additions: exact playbook steps for identifying kernel saturation, safe rollback command sequence, and communication template for customers and internal stakeholders.
Telemetry contract: new metrics (kernel_queue_length, per-tenant-fallback_rate, canary_tail_latency_delta) and thresholds; dashboards and alert rules linked in PRD.
Rollout gating: define fast-fail criteria that abort rollout automatically if canary metrics breach thresholds; manual approval path documented when synthetic/real checks are inconclusive.
Post-release verification: automated smoke for 24h and a 72h human ops review with checklist entries recorded in release notes and incident tracker.
Compatibility note: requirements must work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; provide migration notes if any telemetry is unavailable in Private installs.
acceptance_criteria: PRD text updated and reviewed by SRE and Runtime leads and marked accepted in doc comments.
A matrix mapping each postmortem action item to a verifiable acceptance test exists and is stored as linked artifact (Drive link included in notes).
All acceptance tests are automatable in CI and have one smoke script per scenario that returns clear pass/fail codes.
Dashboards and alerts are defined with exact metric names and thresholds; engineer-run checklist to validate dashboards in staging is present.
Canary gating logic is specified and reviewed by Security and SRE; automated abort path described and validated by a dry run in staging.
Operator runbook has been updated with steps and templates and at least two on-call engineers have practiced the runbook in a tabletop exercise.
Release notes include the safety-belt summary and rollback criteria; rollout will not start until canary tests are passing in staging.

rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): apply PRD changes and runbook to staging; execute synthetic suites against staging cluster.
Stage 1 (canary): deploy to 1% traffic with automated gating; abort on fail and record metrics for 2hr.
Stage 2 (ramped): 10% -> 50% over 6 hours if canary metrics steady; continuous monitoring and human ops checks at each step.
Stage 3 (full): 100% traffic after 24h of stable metrics and successful 72h smoke verification.
If any automated gate fails, immediate rollback to previous serving binary and open a rollback incident; runbook steps executed and RCA planned.
monitoring: Add kernel_queue_length per-host and per-tenant histograms to runtime dashboards.
Track per-tenant fallback_rate and correlate with tenant request patterns.
Synthetic health checks executed every 15m with slack alerts on repeated failures.
Post-deploy canary metric logging persisted for 30 days for retrospective analysis.
